per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: with a lane declared, the inbox slice's prompt carries that lane's latest completed run under its lane name — the failing job's log, or an explicit unread reason when the forge CLI is absent or no run has completed — and says which when the run is green.
tests: the inbox window renders the declared lane's failing run under its lane name
the inbox window renders a lane as unread when the forge CLI is absent
the inbox window renders a lane as unread when no completed run for the tip's branch exists
the inbox window renders a lane whose latest completed run passed as green
notes: No title parser: the run is rendered and the slice's agent takes the titles, as it takes a record's content — a generic parse of a consumer's runner output is the inference the boundary rule fences. Liveness is deliberately not a leg here; the fork is the open question, and this entry ships under every branch of it.

summary: nothing reads the trigger and lane content win32 support now rests on, so a lane that stops running on push to main still reads as supported
acceptance: the suite refuses a workflow whose push trigger drops `main`, or whose windows-latest lane drops one of the four steps the section names.
pins: the CI workflow runs on every push to main
the windows-latest lane runs typecheck, the default test lane, build and the install smoke
notes: Both properties hold on disk today (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so they are pins. The section's support claim is now conditional on the lane running, and the condition is a fact about a committed file that no rung above prose holds.
